protections: Every argument of a FunctionExpression is bound as a placeholder unless the caller explicitly marks a key 'literal'; the docblock states 'all params passed are quoted by default unless explicitly told otherwise' and the literal key is the deliberate exception (Cake/Database/Expression/FunctionExpression.php:25-26,42-53, add() at :92-106, sql() at :120-135).
Identifier quoting is applied to Comparison, OrderByExpression and IdentifierExpression expressions, but FunctionExpression has no branch in the quoter (Cake/Database/IdentifierQuoter.php:63-77).

The only enum-like parameter string in the function factory is normalized by exact-match dispatch instead of interpolation: now($type) returns NOW/CURRENT_DATE/CURRENT_TIME only for 'datetime'/'date'/'time' (Cake/Database/FunctionsTrait.php:156-166).

The advisory's own protection - an allow-list on cast()'s data type, extract()'s date part and dateAdd()'s interval unit - HAS NO SITE at this pin: there is no FunctionsBuilder class and no cast/extract/dateAdd method in the tree; FunctionsTrait (Cake/Database/FunctionsTrait.php:26-168) is the whole function factory, VERSION.txt:19 is 3.0.0-dev, and composer.json:28-32 is a PSR-0 Cake\ => '.' layout with no src/ directory.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: func() is the documented arbitrary-function factory: the name is the SQL function the developer chose to call, not a data parameter, and the published fix documents string/ExpressionInterface parameters as unsafe rather than validating them.

Query declares a func() that is byte-identical to the trait's, so a solver who greps for 'function func' sees two and may fix only the trait one; the visible test exercises only a getObjectForTrait mock of the trait, so hardening Cake/Database/FunctionsTrait.php:37-39 leaves the production Query::func() path (which shadows the trait member because Query.php:38 imports the trait into a class that redeclares func) completely open.

name() is a public mutable setter that the SQL dialects themselves call with the empty string (PostgresDialectTrait.php:101,105; SqliteDialectTrait.php:73), so a check placed in the constructor or in the factory is bypassed by renaming after construction, while a check placed in the setter breaks CONCAT/DATEDIFF compilation.

A string key whose value is 'literal' is the class's documented raw-SQL escape hatch (docblock FunctionExpression.php:42-53) and this is the single choke point every function route passes through; guarding it here rejects the dialects' own literal fragments (' 0 ' at PostgresDialectTrait.php:112,116,120 and "'now'" at SqliteDialectTrait.php:84,87,90).

A string handed to sum/avg/max/min/count IS the SQL expression to aggregate, which must stay unquoted; the repository's own tests require sum('total') to compile to SUM(total) and count('*') to COUNT(*) (FunctionsTraitTest.php:58-60,102-104), so any allow-list that rejects operators or '*' is a regression.

concat()/coalesce()/dateDiff() forward caller-built expression arrays straight into FunctionExpression, where any 'literal' key is raw SQL by contract; the repo's tests rely on concat(['title' => 'literal', ...]) and coalesce(['NULL' => 'literal', ...]) (FunctionsTraitTest.php:113,124; QueryTest.php:1862).

masking: T4 -> T5/T6: a guard on literal keys inside FunctionExpression::add() closes the sum/avg/concat routes but immediately breaks the dialect rewrites (PostgresDialectTrait.php:112,116,120; SqliteDialectTrait.php:84,87,90), which pushes the only workable fix up to the per-method factory layer - the lower-layer trap is only visible once the upper route is fixed.

conflicts.what: A ^[a-zA-Z0-9]+$ style function-name rule enforced in name() is incompatible with the dialects renaming expressions to '' for CONCAT and DATEDIFF (PostgresDialectTrait.php:101,105; SqliteDialectTrait.php:73); the same rule in the constructor is safe because every constructed name in the tree is alphanumeric ('CONCAT','DATEDIFF','DATE','JULIANDAY','LOCALTIMESTAMP','CAST','NOW','CURRENT_DATE','CURRENT_TIME').

A literal-key allow-list coarse enough to close the aggregate and concat routes rejects the whitespace/quoted constants the dialects need (' 0 ' at PostgresDialectTrait.php:112,116,120 and "'now'" at SqliteDialectTrait.php:84,87,90), which breaks now()/CURRENT_DATE/CURRENT_TIME end-to-end (QueryTest.php:1879-1883).

The dialect rewrites use the conjunction slot as SQL glue as well (type(' ||') at PostgresDialectTrait.php:101 and SqliteDialectTrait.php:73, type(' AS ') at PostgresDialectTrait.php:113, type('-') at :106), so a guard on FunctionExpression::add() or on QueryExpression::type() (QueryExpression.php:79-86) must not extend to the conjunction.

fairness_risks: The security rule the traps suggest directly contradicts the class's published contract ('all params passed are quoted by default unless explicitly told otherwise', FunctionExpression.php:25-26,42-53): raw literal fragments are a required, documented feature for aggregate expressions and column names, and the tests enforce it (FunctionsTraitTest.php:58-60,102-104,113,124; FunctionExpressionTest.php:63-67; QueryTest.php:1849-1872).

A function-name allow-list must still accept the empty string, because CONCAT/DATEDIFF are rewritten to a name-less prefix (PostgresDialectTrait.php:101,105; SqliteDialectTrait.php:73); refusing '' breaks compiling every CONCAT and DATEDIFF on PostgreSQL and SQLite.

A literal-key allow-list must still accept surrounding spaces and embedded quotes (' 0 ' and "'now'"), the exact shapes a naive quote/comment filter would reject, because the NOW/CURRENT_DATE/CURRENT_TIME rewrites emit them (PostgresDialectTrait.php:112-120; SqliteDialectTrait.php:84-90).

The advisory's own refused shape 'SIGNED INTEGER' / 'VARCHAR(255)' (screener O5) has no analogue at the pin because cast() does not exist, so a task built here could not exercise the coupled-value behaviour the advisory actually fixes.

now($type) silently returns null for any unknown $type (FunctionsTrait.php:156-166); tightening that path to throw would change existing behaviour for callers that rely on the null return, another easy over-hardening.

design.why: At this pin only three independent groups exist - {T1,T2} function-name validation, {T3} rename-after-check, {T4,T5,T6} literal-argument sink - and they do have the required spread (deepseek: 'the name/expression is arbitrary SQL by design', with a second implementation that makes a trait-only fix look complete; mimo: the dialects' own name('') and ' 0 '/'now' literals plus SUM(total)/COUNT(*) must keep working, so over-hardening is the likely failure). That design is nonetheless not buildable from this candidate: the advisory names FunctionsBuilder::cast/extract/dateAdd, and neither the class nor those methods exist anywhere in the tree (no src/, PSR-0 Cake/ layout per composer.json:28-32, VERSION.txt:19 = 3.0.0-dev), so the published fix cannot be applied and any fix-derived hidden test would call undefined methods. Re-aiming the task at the surviving raw-fragment sites would test an invented policy that contradicts the documented API contract (FunctionExpression.php:25-26,42-53) and the repository's own tests, so a solver could not derive the intended semantics from the report. It only becomes usable after re-pinning to a tree that actually contains src/Database/FunctionsBuilder.php, where the same three groups exist around the advisory's real methods and the M2 duplicate/literal-sink traps still discriminate.
